clue.text: Very wise man, the first to hide face

indicators.note: the very wise man takes the first inside himself, hiding it from view

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
I is the Roman numeral one, the first

explanation.surface: A sage is told to cover his face before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hide' puts I (the first, one) inside V + SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary synonym for a person's face or countenance.

clue.text: Jezebel? Type to want blood, releasing anger

indicators.note: letting go of something, so the anger word is dropped out of the bloodsucker

parts.note: a vampire is the kind of creature that craves blood
ire is another word for anger

explanation.surface: A wicked temptress is a sort who thirsts for blood and lets her temper go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing' takes IRE off the end of VAMPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Jezebel is the Biblical byword for a shameless seductress, which a vamp is; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Composer's deception appearing in woman's dress

indicators.note: the deception shows up within the dress, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sari is a dress worn by women in South Asia
a lie is a deception

explanation.surface: A composer's trickery involves turning up in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: Antonio Salieri was the Italian court composer in Vienna remembered as Mozart's supposed rival; 'appearing in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Salieri was an eighteenth-century Italian composer working in Vienna, so he is a composer by name.

clue.text: City dismal, unknown to be impressive

indicators.note: the unknown is to be turned into the impressive word, a swap of one part for another

parts.note: grey means dull and dismal
Y is a mathematical unknown
noble means grand and impressive

explanation.surface: A city is gloomy and anonymous, yet somehow manages to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' replaces the Y of GREY with NOBLE, leaving GRE + NOBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenoble is a city in the French Alps, an example of the general word.

clue.text: Poor competitor features in heat inadequately — not much good

parts.note: to underdo food is to cook it too little

indicators.note: only a scrap of the word good is used, so just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A weak contestant cooks badly in the heats and achieves little of value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not much' takes only G from 'good'; 'features in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the competitor expected to lose, a poor bet against stronger rivals.

clue.text: Old show number soon getting taken up — a bit of music going round

indicators.note: the musical bit surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a note is a single bit of music

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means written from the bottom upwards, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: ten is a number
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: An old show tune quickly gets picked up, with a snatch of melody going round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting taken up' reads the number and 'soon' upwards as one run, since this is a down clue; 'going round' wraps the bit of music about that run.
explanation.definitionFit: No, No, Nanette is a 1925 musical comedy, famous for Tea for Two, so it is an old show.

clue.text: They go out to ride with 'ounds south of the river

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so this piece follows

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
to ride with hounds is to hunt, with the H dropped as the apostrophe shows

explanation.surface: Hunters head out on horseback with their hounds beyond the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ounds signals the same in 'unt. EXEUNT is the stage direction for several actors leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction meaning that several characters leave the stage.

clue.text: After bumpy ride, Paisley's lot stopped talking

indicators.note: a bumpy ride is jolted about, so the letters of ride are shaken up

parts.note: the DUP, Democratic Unionist Party, was founded and led by Ian Paisley

explanation.surface: After a rough journey, the Northern Irish politicians fell silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumpy' signals the anagram and 'After' puts the party behind it. Ian Paisley founded and led Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry up is an idiom for falling silent, especially forgetting one's lines.

clue.text: Promise of money in Paraguay lacking ultimate support

indicators.note: missing its final letter, so the last letter of the currency goes

parts.note: the guarani is the currency of Paraguay
a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball

explanation.surface: A pledge of South American cash comes without the ultimate backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking ultimate' takes I off GUARANI, leaving GUARAN; TEE completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a formal promise or assurance that something will be done.

clue.text: Small tree in avenue by motorway

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
an allee is a tree-lined avenue, from French

explanation.surface: A little tree grows on a boulevard beside the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLEE (French allée) is an avenue; M comes first, with 'by' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallee is a small, many-stemmed Australian eucalyptus, a kind of low tree.

clue.text: Worms found by girls crossing lake

indicators.note: the lake sits across the join between the two girls, so it goes inside

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
Ida is a second girl's name
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Worms are discovered by girls wading through a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' places the lake at the join between the two names, inside the pair as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Annelida is the phylum of segmented worms, including earthworms and leeches.

clue.text: And is that genetic material?

parts.note: the clue word is three letters which, recombined, make the abbreviation for deoxyribonucleic acid

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the conjunction is a piece of genetic code.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: DNA rearranged ('recombinant') gives AND, the clue's one wordplay word.
explanation.definitionFit: Recombinant DNA is DNA spliced from different sources, genetic material made in the laboratory.

clue.text: An extra No 13 heard? On this part of its route, maybe

definitions.text: On this part of its route, maybe

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, so it is the sound that counts, not the spelling

parts.note: a baker's dozen is thirteen, the extra thirteenth loaf being a baker's treat

explanation.surface: Someone hears of an extra number 13 and wonders where on its route it runs.
explanation.walkthrough: A baker's dozen is 13, so the 13th item is a 'baker's treat', which sounds like BAKER STREET; the London number 13 bus runs along Baker Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Baker Street is a London road served by the number 13 bus, hence part of its route.

clue.text: Game without kids (in bed?) is engaging relations

annotationWithheld.why: Game without kids (in bed?) is engaging relations: IS engaging KIN gives IKINS, but no parse found for SPILL from 'without kids (in bed?)', and no blog for this puzzle was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Game without kids (in bed?) is engaging relations

clue.text: In and out of this may pass spirit or ghost that's disturbed girl

definitions.text: In and out of this may pass spirit

indicators.note: a disturbed ghost is stirred up, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A drink's vessel through which spirits come and go, or a restless spectre that troubled a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's disturbed' is the anagram signal. 'spirit' looks supernatural beside 'ghost' but means liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot glass holds a single measure of spirits, which goes in and is then drunk out of it.

clue.text: Hole produced by spades — amount of soil shifted?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
a pit is a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: Digging with spades makes a hole, measured by the soil moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced by' is a link putting S beside PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a spade's depth of earth, the amount turned over in one dig.

clue.text: Record collections featuring wicked composer

parts.note: arch means mischievous or roguish, as in an arch smile
Charles Ives was an American composer

explanation.surface: A music library includes works by a naughty composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring' is a link. Charles Ives was an early twentieth-century American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical records, a store of documents.

clue.text: Circles made by antelopes, not straight lines

indicators.note: the straight lines are not wanted, so they are struck out

parts.note: oribis are small African antelopes
the letter I looks like a straight line, so two of them stand for straight lines

explanation.surface: Antelopes run in rings rather than straight lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes both I's from ORIBIS, leaving ORBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbs are spheres or circles, as with a planet's orb or a circular path.

clue.text: State of airline facing changes, needing a 50% cutback

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: the changes word must be cut by half, so it keeps only its first five of ten letters

parts.note: variations are changes

explanation.surface: An airline in trouble has to slash its budget by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing a 50% cutback' halves the ten-letter word for changes; 'facing' is a link setting the airline in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Bavaria is a federal state of Germany, an example of the general word.

clue.text: Keep company with female, then restrain wild desire finally

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of restrain are scattered
only the closing letter of desire is used

explanation.surface: Someone spends time with a woman, then has to curb a reckless urge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges RESTRAIN as RATERNIS; 'finally' gives E from 'desire'. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fraternise is to associate in a friendly way, especially with the other side.

clue.text: Put into position with great pomp and ceremony

definitions.meaning: to establish someone in an office or place
as a phrase, done grandly, like a body lying in formal ceremony

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, IN STATE means with formal ceremony, as in lying in state.
explanation.definitionFit: Instate means install in office, and as the phrase in state it means with ceremonial grandeur.

clue.text: Mini designer primarily associated with the smallest bits

parts.note: Mary Quant was the fashion designer credited with popularising the miniskirt

indicators.note: the leading letter only of associated is used

explanation.surface: The miniskirt designer is chiefly connected with tiny bits of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives A from 'associated'; 'with' is a link. 'Mini' looks like the car but is the miniskirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Quanta are the smallest discrete amounts of energy in physics, plural of quantum.

clue.text: Perhaps decided not to involve anyone else in one's life story and died

definitions.text: Perhaps decided not to involve anyone else in one's life story
definitions.meaning: dropped the hired ghostwriter and wrote the memoir oneself

explanation.walkthrough: A ghost is a ghostwriter, so giving up the ghost can mean writing your autobiography yourself; the idiom also means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to breathe one's last, and literally to dispense with a ghostwriter.

clue.text: Boot that is removed may be full of water

indicators.note: taken away, so the letters for that is are dropped

parts.note: a wellie is a rubber Wellington boot
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A boot taken off may be found to be full of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' takes IE off WELLIE. A wellie is a British word for a rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A well is a shaft sunk to reach groundwater, so it is something that holds water.

clue.text: A bishop's given to wrath — someone fiddling with hymn tunes?

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title
anger is wrath

explanation.surface: A bishop loses his temper at a church musician tinkering with the hymns.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) is the title of an Anglican bishop; 'given to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An arranger adapts music for performance, which may mean reworking hymn tunes; 'fiddling' is playful.

clue.text: Calcutta via Teheran? Only some fly

indicators.note: Only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traveller asks about a route from Calcutta through Teheran, flying only part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot or travel by aircraft, a formal word for flying.

clue.text: Fifty workers by the water getting protective coverings

parts.note: the sea is the water
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
ants are workers, from worker ants

explanation.surface: Fifty labourers by the sea are given protective gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'getting' are links; the water piece comes first in the answer although it is last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealants are substances applied as a protective, waterproof coating.

clue.text: Bony duck — cheap buy

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O
a steal is a bargain

explanation.surface: A scrawny duck goes for a bargain price.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is zero in cricket, written O.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is a technical adjective meaning relating to or like bone.
